reviews.reason: The filing covers braces <=3.0.3 and names no first patched release, and 3.0.3 is what the registry publishes as latest, so there is no version to take: the only dependent, micromatch@4.0.8 (also latest), requires braces ^3.0.3. The chains are all Node build and test tooling — metro-file-map > micromatch, reached through @expo/metro > @expo/metro-config > expo and through metro > @react-native/community-cli-plugin > react-native, and jest-haste-map, @jest/core, @jest/transform, jest-config and jest-message-util > micromatch — and no module of braces appears in the exported Hermes bundles, so nothing this repository ships runs it. What the filing describes is unguarded recursion in the AST walkers: a deeply nested brace pattern exhausts the call stack and ends the Node process with a RangeError, and every pattern these callers hand the matcher is a glob this repository or its developer writes — metro's recrawl globs, the testMatch this repository's jest.config.js sets, the coverage globs its Jest preset supplies, and the path argument a jest run is given — while the file paths they test are subjects, which braces never parses, so neither a served catalog nor a device can supply a pattern. Re-review when upstream releases a fixed braces, when micromatch drops the dependency, or by this date.

The filing covers every published release of node-forge, and 1.4.0 is the newest, so no version of the pinned expo resolves without it: expo > @expo/cli > node-forge and expo > @expo/cli > @expo/code-signing-certificates > node-forge. Both callers are Node build tooling — the CLI's macOS keychain code signing and the dev code-signing certificate generator — and no module of node-forge appears in the exported Android, iOS or web bundle, so nothing this repository ships runs it. What the filing describes is a signature-verification defect (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification accepting extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements) reached when the CLI reads a code-signing certificate or request, which in that flow comes from the developer's own machine rather than a remote party. Re-review when upstream releases a fixed node-forge, when the Expo CLI drops the dependency, or by this date.
